index.title: Troubleshooting
index.subtitle: Guided troubleshooting checklists for your engines: 2-stroke outboards and inboard diesels. Always start with the global checklist, it points you to the right sheet.
index.empty: No engine eligible for troubleshooting in your fleet.
index.eligibilityHint: Troubleshooting checklists cover 2-stroke outboards and inboard engines (diesel on a shaft line or saildrive, sterndrives, generator sets). Set the engine family on an engine's page to see it listed here.

firstContactCard.title: Buying used: first contact
firstContactCard.text: Going to see a used engine? Follow the first-contact sheet to assess it on the spot without missing anything.

common.resetConfirm: Reset this checklist? All checked steps for this engine will be unchecked.
common.resetSheetConfirm: Reset this sheet? Its checked steps will be unchecked for this engine.
common.neverDry: This sheet involves starting the engine: always in a water tub or with flushing muffs, never dry. A few seconds dry is enough to destroy the impeller.
common.localStateHint: This sheet is not tied to any engine in your fleet: checkboxes are not saved and start fresh on your next visit.
common.seaCockTitle: Open the sea cock before starting
common.seaCock: This sheet involves starting the engine: make sure the raw water sea cock is open and that water comes out of the exhaust within the first few seconds. With no water, shut down immediately — the impeller is destroyed in seconds.

global.title: Global checklist — the golden rule
global.intro: Compression → Spark → Fuel. Always in that order. Fuel is tested last even though it is the cause in 7 to 8.5 cases out of 10, only because it is the cheapest repair. Without compression, nothing else matters. Steps are ordered from cheapest to most expensive.

flywheel.label: Flywheel turned by hand through 360° — no hard spot

gearshift.label: Gears: propeller free in neutral, resistant in forward and reverse

kill_switch.label: Kill switch in place and in the run position

fresh_fuel.label: Fresh fuel, properly mixed (50:1 unless spec says otherwise), no water

fuel_system.label: Fuel system followed end to end

timing.label: Everything checks out and it still won't run: timing

warnings.waterOnly: Always in a water tub or with flushing muffs. Never dry.

compression.title: Low or uneven compression
compression.intro: Test: spark plugs removed, gauge threaded into the plug hole, 5 to 8 pulls of the starter rope (or 2 to 4 s on the electric starter), on every cylinder, gauge zeroed between readings.

spread_calculated.label: Spread between cylinders calculated
spread_calculated.detail: That is criterion #1, not the raw value.

model_spec.label: Model spec checked
model_spec.detail: Some Johnson/Evinrude 9.5s run perfectly fine at 60–68 PSI.

retest_after_run.label: Engine sat unused for a long time? Retest after a few hours of running

retest_after_head.label: After any cylinder head removal: recheck once torqued to spec

warnings.gauges: Gauges vary wildly: a €20 model reads 10 to 15 PSI lower than a professional one. Compare cylinders against each other, never numbers from two different gauges.

notes.over_spread: If the spread exceeds 12%: rings, scored cylinder, or head gasket. That is the expensive repair — when buying, negotiate very low or walk away.

kill_circuit.label: Kill circuit: disconnect the black/yellow wire at the power pack and retest
kill_circuit.detail: Spark back = fault in the stop circuit (key switch, harness, corroded terminals).

plugs.label: New spark plugs, gap checked with a tool (they are not set at the factory), same brand everywhere

coils.label: Coils: visual inspection of the gel on the back
coils.detail: Dry, cracked, or melted = dead coil. It is the ignition component that fails most often.

rectifier.label: Rectifier: disconnect the yellow wires and retest (2 seconds, rare case but free)

cranking_rpm.label: Cranking speed ≥ 250 rpm (otherwise battery, cables, or starter)

grounds.label: Grounds clean, corrosion-free, tight — especially the coil grounds

model_id.label: Model + year identified on crowleymarine.com (e.g. J50PLEA = Johnson 50 hp 1999)

cdi_measures.label: Stator / timer base / power pack measured in ohms per the CDI guide
cdi_measures.detail: Sample readings: stator brown ↔ brown/yellow 650–850 Ω (CDI) or 750–950 Ω (OEM); timer base white ↔ green and white ↔ blue 25–30 Ω. A value inside either range is enough.

warnings.weak_spark: A spark visible on the tester can still be too weak under compression. If everything else checks out and one cylinder is not firing, try a coil.

notes.triage_all: Triage rule: no spark on any cylinder → look for what is shared (kill switch, stator, power pack).
notes.triage_one: No spark on a single cylinder → that cylinder's plug or coil.
notes.dva: Peak voltages require a DVA adapter. If the resistance is good, the voltage almost always is too.

fuel.title: Fuel supply (culprit #1)
fuel.intro: Physically follow the path: tank → hose + primer bulb → filter → pump → carburetor → reed valves.

fresh_fuel.label: Fuel less than a month old, properly mixed, no water

black_hose_only.label: Black automotive fuel hose only
black_hose_only.detail: Grey hoses have a liner that ethanol dissolves (debris in the carburetor).

primer_bulb.label: Primer bulb fitted following the arrows, it must get completely firm

air_leaks.label: Hunt for air leaks: every clamp, every quick connector

filter_direction.label: Filter clean and fitted the right way (arrow)

pump_test.label: Pump test: engine dies after 20–60 s? Restart while squeezing the primer bulb continuously
pump_test.detail: If it stays alive on the bulb → pump is dead.

pump_replace.label: Replace with a new assembled pump rather than a kit

carb_photos.label: Photos of hoses and linkages before disassembly

carb_removal.label: Removal: air box, hoses, linkage, 2 nuts

carb_disassembly.label: Disassembly: bowl, float, needle valve, every jet

mixture_screw_count.label: Mixture screw: count the turns while backing it out

carb_cleaner.label: Carb cleaner in every hole and orifice, generously — nothing can be damaged

cork_float.label: Cork float → replace with a plastic one outright

float_level.label: Float level even on every axis (adjust the tab)

blow_test.label: Blow test
blow_test.detail: Bowl down → air passes; carburetor upside down → no air passes.

reassembly.label: Reassembly, then mixture screw adjustment
reassembly.detail: Screw gently seated, backed out 1 to 1¼ turn, fine-tuned by ¼ turn with 20–30 s to react.

reed_backfire.label: Fuel spitting back out of the carburetor throat, or backfiring?

reed_backlight.label: Reeds against the light: light visible between the petals = replace

choke_only.symptom: Only runs with the choke on

leaking.symptom: Fuel dripping while squeezing the primer bulb
leaking.cause: Stuck float / needle valve no longer sealing

flooding.cause: Worn needle valve, punctured float, enrichment solenoid powered permanently (~5.5 ± 1.5 Ω)

dry_plugs.symptom: Dry plugs, no fuel at all

telltale_nipple.label: Tell-tale nipple: insect nests, mud — run a thin wire through the nipple and its hose

thermostat.label: Thermostat: remove it and run again
thermostat.detail: 5 minutes, it settles the question immediately. Corroded shut = classic.

impeller.label: Impeller: curled, dry, or cracked vanes = replace (~€15, THE #1 maintenance item)
impeller.detail: Gearcase in reverse before removal, do not lose the key, liquid soap on reassembly.

drill_test.label: Test before refitting the gearcase: drill on the driveshaft → water must squirt out of the outlet port

water_tube.label: New impeller but still nothing? Misaligned copper water tube or clogged internal passages
water_tube.detail: The grommet must seat properly. Garden hose test into the water tube: water must come out at the thermostat housing.

water_jackets.label: Blocked water jackets (sand, scale): remove the head cover, sometimes the powerhead
water_jackets.detail: Heaviest level, everything else must be ruled out first.

ir_thermometer.label: Check: infrared thermometer on the head near the spark plug

warnings.no_thermostat: Do not run without a thermostat: an engine running too cold wears just like one running too hot.

notes.used_engine: Worth remembering: on a used engine "that overheats", the previous owner has often already replaced the impeller and removed the thermostat with no result. Do not trust past repairs: run the checklist again from the top.

gear_oil.label: Milky or grey gearcase oil = water → seals to redo

shear_pin.label: Slipping propeller, small engines: broken shear pin
shear_pin.detail: It must stick out in a T on both sides of the hub — a €3 part.

spun_hub.label: Slipping propeller, bigger engines: spun hub
spun_hub.detail: Feels like cavitation under acceleration → re-hub or replace.

shift_linkage.label: Stiff or dead gear shifting: check the linkage and cables first, before opening the gearcase

corroded_gearcase.label: Gearcase welded on by corrosion: gentle escalation
corroded_gearcase.detail: Bolts first (penetrating oil + heat), then progressively bigger putty knives in the parting line, then a progressive pry bar.

grease_splines.label: On reassembly: grease splines and threads

warnings.cold_shift: In severe cold, the shift rod becomes brittle.

battery.label: Battery charged, terminals clean and tight — always start there

solenoid_jump.label: Click without rotation: jump the solenoid's two large posts
solenoid_jump.detail: Starter spins → dead solenoid. It does not spin → dead starter.

solenoid_welded.label: Welded solenoid: with a multimeter, any continuity between the posts with the key out = stuck contacts → replace

runaway_starter.label: Starter that keeps spinning with the engine running: disconnect the battery immediately
runaway_starter.detail: Short circuit in the relay or the button.

connections.label: Connections redone properly: crimped terminals then heat-shrink tubing

trim_wiring.label: Trim dead at one station only: follow the blue/green wires
trim_wiring.detail: A cut wire is more likely than a dead trim motor. At-sea workaround: manual tilt release screw.

battery_switch.label: Battery switch on, start bank separate from the service bank
battery_switch.detail: A flat service bank must not stop you starting: if it does, the combiner or the wiring is at fault.

start_battery_load.label: Start battery tested under load, not just with a voltmeter
start_battery_load.detail: A tired battery reads 12.6 V at rest and collapses the moment you crank: only a load test exposes it.

glow_plugs.label: Pre-heating: timer and glow plugs working
glow_plugs.detail: A diesel that starts well hot and refuses cold points to pre-heating before fuel supply.

start_relay.label: Start relay and switch: audible click, sound contacts
start_relay.detail: A click with no rotation points to the starter or its cables; no click at all, to the switch and its supply.

alternator_belt.label: Alternator belt: tension and no slipping
alternator_belt.detail: Engine off, key removed. A slipping belt squeals and leaves black dust.

alternator_output.label: Charging voltage measured with the engine running
alternator_output.detail: With no measurable charge the battery drains outing after outing, and the failure happens far from the pontoon.

panel_alarm.label: Panel alarms (temperature, oil pressure) live with the ignition on
panel_alarm.detail: These alarms must sound with the key on and the engine stopped. Silent, they will warn you of nothing.

timing.title: Timing and link & sync
timing.intro: When: after a carburetor rebuild, after replacing the timer base / stator / power pack, after touching any linkage, or on an unknown used engine showing the symptoms below. Not systematically.

shop_manual.label: Shop manual for the model in hand
shop_manual.detail: No generic value replaces the engine's spec.

cam_roller.label: Cam follower roller present and intact (often broken on old engines)

fast_start_modules.label: "Fast start" / S.L.O.W. modules disconnected if the manual says so

tdc_pointer.label: Timing pointer verified against true TDC of cylinder #1
tdc_pointer.detail: Two positions with identical rod depth: TDC is in the middle.

wot_stop.label: Wide-open-throttle stop: butterflies horizontal
wot_stop.detail: The stop screw ends the travel, never the carburetor's internal stops.

max_advance.label: Max advance set to spec, never beyond
max_advance.detail: Orders of magnitude: ~34° BTDC old Mercury crossflow, ~21° direct charge, 19–28° OMC crossflow.

pickup_timing.label: Throttle pickup: cam mark aligned with the center of the roller
pickup_timing.detail: The throttle starts opening around 3–5° BTDC.

warm_mixture.label: Engine warm in the water: mixture fine-tuned by ¼ turn

idle_rpm.label: Idle 700–800 rpm in neutral, 550–650 rpm in gear

cable_preload.label: Cable reconnected with a slight preload against the idle stop

no_start.symptom: Won't start despite compression + spark + clean carburetor

high_idle.symptom: Idle too high, screw at its stop

acceleration_gap.lead: Pickup too early or too late

warnings.max_advance: Excessive max advance burns holes in pistons. When in doubt, set it retarded.

notes.single_carb: Single carburetor (4–15 hp): the "sync" part disappears. If the engine has no adjustable advance stop, it comes down to cam/roller alignment + mixture screw + idle stop, no timing light.

first_contact.title: First contact (buying used)
first_contact.intro: To run on the spot, in front of the seller, before any negotiation.

gearshift.label: Gears: neutral free, forward and reverse resistant

compression.label: Compression on every cylinder
compression.detail: A seller who refuses this test is often hiding something.

gear_oil.label: Gearcase oil drained a little: milky = water

external_tank.label: Clean external tank with fresh fuel — never the boat's own

primer_bulb.label: Primer bulb that firms up, no leak, no air noise

start_listen.label: Start it and listen to how it behaves

notes.deal_breakers: Deal breakers: seized piston, gearcase that will not shift.

inboard_cooling.title: Overheating and cooling
inboard_cooling.intro: An inboard cools in two stages: raw water drawn from under the hull cools a closed circuit, then leaves through the exhaust. Follow the raw water in order — that is almost always where it blocks — before touching the closed circuit.

sections.raw_water: Raw water circuit, in flow order

strainer.label: Strainer opened, basket cleaned, lid seal in good condition
strainer.detail: A hardened seal lets air in: the pump loses its prime with no visible dirt at all.

hose_collapse.label: Suction hose neither collapsed nor sagging
hose_collapse.detail: A hose that collapses at high revs causes overheating only under load.

impeller.label: Impeller removed: vanes supple, none deformed or missing
impeller.detail: An impeller is replaced on wear, not on failure — hardened or set vanes mean it is at the end of its life.

impeller_debris.label: Missing vanes searched for downstream (heat exchanger, elbow)
impeller_debris.detail: A piece of impeller carried downstream blocks the exchanger: while it is there, the overheating comes back.

pump_cover.label: Pump cover flat, unscored, new gasket on reassembly

coolant_level.label: Closed circuit level and coolant condition
coolant_level.detail: Cold engine only. Brownish or oily coolant points to an internal leak.

belt.label: Pump drive belt: tension, condition, alignment

thermostat.label: Thermostat removed and tested, or replaced
thermostat.detail: Stuck closed: immediate overheating. Stuck open: the engine never reaches temperature.

heat_exchanger.label: Exchanger core: scaling, deposits, blockage
heat_exchanger.detail: Overheating that builds slowly, only under load, points to the exchanger before the impeller.

anodes.label: Circuit anodes checked and replaced when consumed
anodes.detail: A forgotten anode ends up in pieces inside the core, which it then blocks in turn.

exhaust_elbow.label: Exhaust elbow free of scale and corrosion

no_water.symptom: No water at the exhaust on start-up
no_water.reading: The raw water circuit is not drawing
no_water.check: Sea cock, strainer, lid seal, impeller

water_no_alarm.reading: Water circulates, heat exchange no longer happens
water_no_alarm.check: Thermostat, scaled exchanger, closed circuit level

steam.symptom: Steam or boiling water at the exhaust
steam.check: Impeller, collapsed hose, scaled elbow. Shut the engine down.

slow_rise.reading: The circuit copes at idle, not beyond
slow_rise.check: Heat exchanger, slipping belt, exhaust elbow

warnings.hotPressurisedCircuit: Never open the cap of a hot, pressurised cooling circuit: steam and boiling coolant come out all at once. Wait until it has fully cooled down.
warnings.engineOffBeforeBelt: Shut the engine down and remove the key before touching a belt or a pulley.
warnings.neverRunDry: Never run the engine with the sea cock closed, not even for a few seconds: the impeller is destroyed before the alarm sounds.

notes.impeller_interval: The impeller is a wear part: most engine makers rate it for a season or two, and a spare on board beats a new one at the pontoon. See your model's service manual for the exact interval.

diesel_fuel.title: Fuel circuit
diesel_fuel.intro: On a leisure diesel, fuel supply is the leading cause of failure, and it is almost always water or deposits from the bottom of the tank. Follow the circuit in order, from the tank to the injectors.

tank_valve.label: Tank valve open, actual level sufficient

prefilter_bowl.label: Pre-filter bowl drained: no water, no sludge
prefilter_bowl.detail: Water settles at the bottom, clearer and denser than the fuel. Drain until only fuel comes out.

prefilter_element.label: Pre-filter element replaced if clogged
prefilter_element.detail: Note the date: an element that clogs within hours points to a dirty tank, not a faulty filter.

engine_filter.label: Engine fuel filter replaced, with a new seal

bleed.label: Circuit bled following the service manual procedure
bleed.detail: A diesel will not restart while air remains: bleed in the order the manufacturer gives, from the filter towards the pump.

air_leak.label: Air leak searched for on the suction side
air_leak.detail: Fittings, filter seals, porous hoses: the engine can draw air without a single drop of fuel leaking out.

lift_pump.label: Lift pump: flow verified
lift_pump.detail: Hand priming that is stiff or offers no resistance, and no flow: the pump or its diaphragm is at fault.

stop_solenoid.label: Stop control (solenoid or cable) in the run position
stop_solenoid.detail: An engine that cranks normally, never fires, with a healthy fuel circuit: look at the stop control first.

injector_return.label: Injector return flow checked
injector_return.detail: An unusually heavy return points to a worn injector. Injector testing and calibration is workshop work.

tank_bottom.label: Tank bottom inspected if clogging keeps recurring
tank_bottom.detail: Filters blocking one after another: it is the tank that needs cleaning, not the filter that needs changing.

starts_then_stalls.symptom: Starts then stalls after a few minutes
starts_then_stalls.check: Clogged pre-filter, air leak, tank vent

power_loss_swell.reading: Deposits from the tank bottom are stirred back up

no_start_after_filter.symptom: Will not restart after a filter change
no_start_after_filter.reading: Air is still in the circuit
no_start_after_filter.check: Full bleed following the manual procedure

hunting.reading: Irregular supply or air being drawn in
hunting.check: Air leak on the suction side, partially clogged filter

warnings.highPressureInjection: Never loosen a high-pressure fitting with the engine running: a diesel injector jet goes through skin and causes serious injury, often with no immediate pain. All work on the injection system is done with the engine stopped.
warnings.fuelAndHotParts: Fuel sprayed onto a hot manifold ignites. Shut the engine down, let it cool, and keep absorbent material within reach.

notes.diesel_bug: The micro-organisms that grow at the water-fuel interface ("diesel bug") form the black sludge found in filters. Keeping the tank full limits condensation, and therefore the water they live on.

diesel_smoke.title: Smoke: black, white or blue
diesel_smoke.intro: Smoke colour is the fastest sorting aid on a diesel: it does not name the fault, but it points at the family to explore. Read it with a hot engine under load, not at idle on the pontoon.

color_identified.label: Colour identified under load, engine hot
color_identified.detail: Black = combustion, white = water or injection, blue = oil. See the table above.

air_filter.label: Air filter and engine bay ventilation clear
air_filter.detail: An engine starved of air smokes black: it is the cheapest check, do it first.

overload.label: Propeller and load suited: the engine reaches its maximum revs
overload.detail: An over-pitched propeller or a fouled hull makes it smoke black constantly and wears the engine.

coolant_loss.label: Closed circuit level tracked over several outings
coolant_loss.detail: Persistent white smoke with a dropping level: water is reaching combustion — stop there and have it checked.

oil_level_rising.label: Engine oil level: neither rising nor milky
oil_level_rising.detail: A level that rises on its own means water or fuel in the sump. Do not go out.

cold_start_only.label: Smoke present on cold start only, or all the time
cold_start_only.detail: A little white for the first few seconds when cold is normal; the same cloud when hot is not.

black.reading: Incomplete combustion: too much fuel or not enough air
black.check: Air filter, engine bay ventilation, over-pitched propeller, exhaust back pressure

white.reading: Water in combustion, or unburnt fuel
white.check: Closed circuit level, head gasket, injection. Briefly, when cold, it is normal.

blue.check: Oil level too high, piston rings, valve guides. Internal wear: workshop.

warnings.whiteSmokeMeansWater: Persistent white smoke when hot, together with a dropping coolant level, means water in the cylinders. Do not carry on cruising: have it checked before going out again.

notes.cold_start_haze: Every numeric value — compression pressure, injector setting, opacity — belongs to your model's service manual. This table points you in a direction, it does not measure anything.

wet_exhaust.title: Wet exhaust and waterlock
wet_exhaust.intro: An inboard exhaust carries gases and raw water together. When it blocks, sags or corrodes, water can find its way back to the engine: the most expensive failure on this list, and the most avoidable.

elbow_corrosion.label: Exhaust elbow removed and inspected: corrosion, scaling
elbow_corrosion.detail: It is the wear part of the exhaust. A holed elbow sends water into the engine through the exhaust.

elbow_injection.label: Elbow water injection point clear
elbow_injection.detail: Scaled up, it raises back pressure and temperature with no other symptom.

waterlock_full.label: Waterlock emptied and not cracked
waterlock_full.detail: After several failed start attempts it fills up: empty it before cranking again.

hose_sag.label: Exhaust hose supported, with no low point where water sits
hose_sag.detail: A sagging hose forms a trap and holds water, which eventually finds its way back.

swan_neck.label: Swan neck high enough above the waterline
swan_neck.detail: It is what stops the sea entering through the exhaust outlet at anchor or downwind.

siphon_break.label: Siphon break (anti-siphon loop) clear
siphon_break.detail: Blocked, it lets the circuit siphon and fill the engine while stopped.

clamps.label: Doubled stainless clamps, with no trace of rust

warnings.waterInCylinders: Never keep cranking when the engine will not start: each attempt sends water into the exhaust, and that water can reach the cylinders. After three unsuccessful attempts, close the sea cock and empty the waterlock.
warnings.carbonMonoxide: An exhaust leaking into the engine bay releases carbon monoxide into the boat: it is odourless and lethal. Any leak is fixed before going out, and a CO detector on board is not a luxury.

notes.elbow_interval: The exhaust elbow is a consumable, not a lifetime part: most engine makers rate it for a few hundred hours or a few seasons. See your model's service manual.

gearbox.title: Gearbox
gearbox.intro: No engagement, jerky shifts, noise on engaging: before suspecting the gearbox itself, check the oil and the control. The vast majority of engagement faults are solved on the cable or the level.

oil_level.label: Oil level checked following the manufacturer's procedure
oil_level.detail: Some gearboxes are checked hot and just after running: the method changes the reading, follow the service manual.

oil_color.label: Oil appearance: neither milky nor burnt, no particles
oil_color.detail: Milky = water, through the oil cooler. Brown and burnt = slipping plates.

control_cable.label: Control cable: outer in good condition, free travel, clevis tight
control_cable.detail: A seized cable or a loose clevis stops the gearbox reaching its engagement detent.

lever_travel.label: Lever travel: the gearbox arm reaches both stops
lever_travel.detail: Check at the gearbox, not at the throttle lever: the adjustment is made at the arm.

damper_plate.label: Damper plate: metallic noise at idle in neutral
damper_plate.detail: A rattle that disappears when engaging points to the damper plate, between engine and gearbox.

output_seal.label: Output shaft seal dry, with no weeping
output_seal.detail: An oil trace under the coupling often comes from here, not from the engine.

oil_cooler.label: Gearbox oil cooler checked
oil_cooler.detail: It is where raw water gets into the oil when the core is holed.

warnings.noEngagementUnderLoad: Do not force an engagement with the engine revving, or engage at high revs: the damper plate and the plates will not take it. A load test is done short-tied alongside, on sound lines, at low revs.

notes.oil_spec: Gearbox oil is not always engine oil — some models call for automatic transmission fluid. The exact specification is in the service manual.

shaft_line.title: Shaft line and stuffing box
shaft_line.intro: The stuffing box is the one point on the shaft line where water comes in on purpose. Vibration, heat or water ingress: the same causes come back — worn packing, cutless bearing, alignment.

packing_drip.label: Drip rate matching the manufacturer's setting
packing_drip.detail: A traditional stuffing box should drip slightly while running. Tightened dry, it heats up and destroys the shaft.

packing_tightening.label: Gland nut and lock nut tight, with no play
packing_tightening.detail: Tighten in small quarter turns, with the boat afloat, checking the temperature after a few minutes.

packing_age.label: Packing age known, replacement planned
packing_age.detail: Hardened packing cannot be recovered by tightening: it scores the shaft instead of sealing it.

cutless_bearing.label: Cutless bearing: vertical shaft play in the bracket
cutless_bearing.detail: Play you can feel by hand means a worn bearing — vibration and shaft wear follow.

shaft_play.label: Shaft straight, with no wear mark or corrosion at the hull fitting

alignment.label: Engine to shaft alignment checked with the boat afloat
alignment.detail: Alignment is checked afloat and rigged: the hull works, a check ashore is worthless.

propeller_fouling.label: Propeller clean, blades free of impact damage or distortion
propeller_fouling.detail: A propeller fouled by a line or bent by an impact gives a clear vibration, proportional to the revs.

warnings.floodingRisk: Water coming in at the stuffing box is a leak: it cannot be repaired at sea if it worsens. Keep something to plug it within reach, know where your bilge pump is, and head back if the flow increases.
warnings.engineOffBeforeShaft: Shut the engine down, remove the key and lock the shaft before working on the shaft line: a shaft driven by the current turns even when stopped.

notes.dripless_variants: Dripless shaft seals do not drip and are checked differently: bellows, air purge after launching, bellows replacement date. Follow the manufacturer's instructions, not the drip rule.

saildrive.title: Saildrive
saildrive.intro: The saildrive goes through the hull: its diaphragm is the only barrier between the sea and the boat. This is the sheet where preventive maintenance matters more than diagnosis — an out-of-date diaphragm is replaced before it leaks, not after.

diaphragm_date.label: Diaphragm fitting date known and within the manufacturer's limit
diaphragm_date.detail: The diaphragm has an expiry date, often seven years, independent of how it looks. Record the fitting date: without it, nobody knows.

diaphragm_condition.label: Diaphragm inspected: no cracking, swelling or signs of ageing
diaphragm_condition.detail: A diaphragm can look sound and still be out of date — appearance never replaces the date.

water_alarm.label: Water-between-diaphragms alarm tested
water_alarm.detail: On twin-diaphragm installations it is what warns you the first one has failed. Test it: a dead alarm protects nothing.

oil_emulsion.label: Leg oil not emulsified
oil_emulsion.detail: Milky, coffee-coloured oil means water past the seals: a haul-out is needed.

anodes.label: Leg anodes checked and replaced when consumed
anodes.detail: An aluminium leg with no anode corrodes quickly, and corrosion cannot be undone.

paint_compatibility.label: Antifouling compatible with an aluminium leg
paint_compatibility.detail: Copper-based antifouling applied straight onto aluminium triggers galvanic corrosion. Use a product made for legs.

gaiter_clamps.label: Diaphragm clamps in place, stainless, free of corrosion

warnings.diaphragmExpiry: A saildrive diaphragm is not an ordinary wear part: it is a safety item with an expiry date. An out-of-date diaphragm, however perfect it looks, is a major flooding risk — replace it at the interval the manufacturer gives, without waiting for a symptom.
warnings.floodingRisk: Water coming in at the leg is dealt with ashore. If you find water in the engine bay around the saildrive, head back and have the boat lifted.

notes.haul_out_required: Replacing the diaphragm requires a haul-out and removal of the leg: plan it into the yard schedule rather than discovering it at survey.

ai.title: AI assistant — troubleshooting
ai.disclaimer: The AI recommends, it does not decide: its advice does not replace your engine model's service manual.
ai.empty: Describe the failure symptoms, or run an analysis of your checklist progress.
ai.placeholder: E.g.: the engine starts then stalls after 30 seconds, the primer bulb stays soft…

globalInboard.title: Inboard global checklist — before dismantling anything
globalInboard.intro: A diesel needs clean air, clean fuel and cooling. Steps are ordered from cheapest to most expensive: everything you can check by hand, with no tool and nothing to dismantle, comes first. That is almost always where the fault is.

battery_switch.label: Battery switch on, terminals clean and tight
battery_switch.detail: A green terminal or a forgotten battery switch imitates a dead starter perfectly.

sea_cock.label: Raw water sea cock open
sea_cock.detail: First reflex after winter storage or a haul-out: it is the most common oversight.

strainer.label: Strainer (raw water filter) clean, lid properly tightened

raw_water_flow.label: Water at the exhaust within seconds of starting
raw_water_flow.detail: No water: shut down at once, do not wait for the temperature alarm.

coolant_level.label: Closed circuit level checked, engine cold
coolant_level.detail: A level that drops with no visible leak often ends up in the oil or at the exhaust.

belt.label: Alternator and pump belt: tension and condition
belt.detail: Engine off, key removed. Black dust under the belt points to a misalignment.

oil_level.label: Engine oil level and appearance
oil_level.detail: Milky or over-full: water or fuel has reached the sump — do not start.

fuel_supply.label: Enough fuel on board, tank valve open

prefilter_bowl.label: Pre-filter bowl: no water, no deposits
prefilter_bowl.detail: Water shows at the bottom of the bowl, denser and clearer than the fuel.

exhaust_smoke.label: Exhaust smoke colour on start-up and under load

bilge_dry.label: Bilge dry under the engine and at the hull fitting
bilge_dry.detail: Salt water under the engine never comes from nowhere: find the source before going out.

warnings.hotPressurisedCircuit: Never open the cap of a hot, pressurised cooling circuit: steam and boiling coolant come out all at once. Wait until the engine has fully cooled down.
warnings.engineOffBeforeBelt: Shut the engine down and remove the key before touching a belt, a pulley or the coupling — an accidental start takes a hand off.
